Speed up your device by tuning animation scales, screen density, battery behaviour and hidden developer settings, all from one place and without root.

Animation speed, screen density and battery behaviour are protected by Android, so the app needs one special permission before it can change them. You grant it once, in about two minutes, using a free helper app called Shizuku or a single command from a computer. We will walk you through every step.
Until then the app can show your current settings but not change them. You can start the guided setup any time from the home screen or from Settings.
Battery tweaks change how aggressively Android sleeps, throttles and freezes apps. There is no single best value. It depends on your device, your ROM and the apps you use.

Change one thing at a time, then use your device normally for a day and compare. Aggressive settings can drain your battery faster, delay notifications, or stop background apps and alarms from working.
Manufacturers modify Android heavily. Some tweaks silently do nothing on your device, some are reverted by the system, and some need a reboot before they take effect.
If something misbehaves, use the reset option in the relevant section or in Settings to return to stock values. When in doubt, note down what you changed before changing it.

What is this and why do I need it?
Why can\'t the app just change my settings?

The settings this app tunes (animation speed, screen density, battery behaviour) are protected by Android. No normal app is allowed to change them, no matter who made it. Your phone needs to hand out one special permission first.
Shizuku is a small, free, open-source helper app. It is the standard way to hand that permission to apps like this one without rooting your phone. Millions of people use it, and it is not made by us.
Is it safe? Does it root my phone?
It does not root your phone and it does not modify Android. Shizuku only stays active until you restart your phone, and you can revoke this app\'s access from inside Shizuku at any time.
On Android 11 and newer, no. Your phone can start Shizuku by itself using wireless debugging. On older versions you need to plug into a computer once.
How do you want to set it up?

Open About phone, find Build number and tap it seven times. Your phone will say you are now a developer. If it is already on, skip this.
In Developer options, switch Wireless debugging on and keep Wi-Fi connected. Accept the warning your phone shows.
Open Shizuku and tap Start under the wireless debugging section, then pair when it asks. It is running once Shizuku shows a green message at the top.
Shizuku will ask whether Custom Animator may use it. Tap Allow.
